sections.h2: Is a quick sale realistic for an Easton house?
sections.html:
It is. Easton owners choose among an agent listing, a sale without an agent, and an as-is cash purchase, and the house's condition, any tenants and your closing date usually settle which one. Deferred repairs, a tenant lease or a clouded inheritance are the usual reasons an owner here looks at cash.

Easton is the seat of Northampton County and the eastern end of the Lehigh Valley, where the Lehigh River joins the Delaware. Allentown lies 14 miles to the southwest, Philadelphia 51 miles south and New York City 64 miles east. The Delaware marks the city's eastern edge, and Phillipsburg, New Jersey, sits across it, so some buyers commute over the bridges.

sections.h2: What should I know about Easton's districts and roads?
sections.html:
Easton's four districts are Downtown, College Hill, South Side and West Ward. Census QuickFacts lists 4.26 square miles of land and 6,597.9 people per square mile in 2020, so houses sit tightly together. Downtown is low ground at the river junction with hills rising north, west and south. Lafayette College anchors College Hill, and South Easton, across the Lehigh, was its own borough until 1898.

  • Roads: US 22, the Lehigh Valley Thruway, crosses the middle of the city. PA 611 hugs the Delaware, and PA 248 begins where those two meet. I-78 touches the southeast corner, but its nearest interchange is in Williams Township.
  • Bridges: the Northampton Street Bridge and the Easton and Phillipsburg Toll Bridge connect to New Jersey.
  • Downtown landmarks: Centre Square, the Crayola Experience and the National Canal Museum.
  • Weather: winters bring about 30 inches of snow, the hardiness zone is 6b, and the record low is minus 15 degrees Fahrenheit, so inspectors look at roofs, gutters and plumbing in older houses.
  • Schools: Easton Area School District covers the city, Forks and Palmer townships and part of Lower Mount Bethel, and its high school is in Palmer Township.

sections.h2: How did Easton get its housing and its reputation?
sections.html:
Easton was named in 1752 for the Easton Neston estate of Thomas Penn's wife's family, and the Lenape called the place Lechauwitank, the Place at the Forks. The Delaware and Lehigh canals made it a coal transfer point in the 19th century, and railroads followed the same corridor. Historians of angling credit an Easton gunsmith, Samuel Phillipe, with the six-strip split-cane fly rod in 1845.

The city's population peaked at 35,632 in 1950, fell to 26,027 by 1980 and has climbed since to 28,127 in 2020. Easton Area School District reported about 8,289 students in 2020 to 2021 across seven elementary schools, a middle school campus in Forks Township and the high school. Crayola's maker is based in nearby Forks Township, and Larry Holmes Drive honors the city's heavyweight champion. Buyers value these town details, so mention what you know of your block's history in the listing or the offer conversation.

sections.h2: How do Easton housing costs compare with local income?
sections.html:
On paper Easton is affordable: an owner's home has a median value of $196,300 for 2020 to 2024, set against household income of $69,348. Owners live in just 44.5% of the city's homes, and the population grew 8.2% from the 2020 base to 30,402 in July 2025.

sections.h2: Which city offices touch an Easton sale?
sections.html:
Start with Code Enforcement, then the Historic District Commission, then the rental licensing desk if anyone rents the house. Code Enforcement applies the city Property Maintenance Code and the Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code, and it can tell you whether permits on your address are still open.

  • Permits: building, enlarging, altering, repairing, moving or demolishing a structure, changing its use, or installing electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems all need one.
  • Historic review: facade and signage work may also need a certificate of appropriateness from the Historic District Commission.
  • Occupancy cap: a single housekeeping unit may hold no more than three unrelated people, and an Occupancy Limitations Certificate states the limit for each dwelling unit.
  • Rental paperwork: an owner who rents files each tenant's name and address with the Rental Licensing Officer, and a moving permit comes from the Finance Department.
  • Fire check: the fire inspector will do a free fire safety inspection if you doubt a building has the required smoke detectors.

For a rented house, gather the lease, rental license papers and tenant form in one folder. A buyer's attorney will ask for them.

sections.h2: What taxes and recording steps come with an Easton sale?
sections.html:
Expect separate bills from the city, the county and the school district. Easton levies 24.95 mills on the value the Northampton County Assessment Office sets, and residents pay a city earned income tax of 1.45% plus 0.5% to Easton Area School District, for 1.95% in all.

The county mailed 2026 bills in mid-January, with the discount ending March 31 and the face amount due June 1. Taxes still unpaid at the close of business on January 31 of the next year pass to the Tax Claim Bureau, which meant January 31, 2027 for the 2026 bill. Clear any balance from the sale proceeds.

The state's realty transfer tax is 1% of value, and the law holds the grantor and the grantee jointly liable. The Recorder of Deeds, at (610) 829-6210, takes it with any local tax at recording, and the city's tax list includes a real estate transfer tax. Request the combined rate for your price before you sign a contract.

The county's 2026 appeal hearings ran from August 5 through October 29. For the present filing deadline, ask the Assessment Division on the second floor of the courthouse at 669 Washington Street. School homestead exclusions come from Act 72 of 2004, so an owner-occupant should ask the school district how the exclusion is handled when the deed changes.

sections.h2: What must an Easton seller tell the buyer?
sections.html:
Pennsylvania's disclosure rule, 68 Pa.C.S. section 7303, reaches anyone selling one to four dwelling units. The seller gives the buyer a completed, signed and dated statement ahead of signing the sales agreement. The state form has 16 topics, from the roof and basement to hazardous substances and legal title problems.

If a seller willfully or negligently skips a duty, the buyer's actual damages are owed, and suit must start within two years of final settlement (section 7311). An executor or other fiduciary selling for an estate is outside the chapter (section 7302). Paying cash earns the buyer no exemption.

sections.h2: When is cash the better route for an Easton house?
sections.html:
Cash fits best when condition, occupancy or timing would stall a listing. Examples from Easton's housing mix:

  • A house left by a relative that no heir wants to keep.
  • A rental where the unit or the license paperwork needs attention.
  • Open permits or code notices that scare off buyers who depend on a mortgage.
  • Roof, plumbing or heating damage after a hard winter.
  • A job transfer, divorce or court date that fixes your move.

Weigh any cash figure against what a listing nets after repairs, concessions and transfer tax. To get a figure for an Easton address, call or text with the details, including tenants and any open code items.

faqs.q: What controls the speed of a cash closing in Easton?
faqs.a: Title work and the date you choose control it, since there is no loan to underwrite. The deed then goes to the Northampton County Recorder of Deeds, and taxes or liens come out of the proceeds.

faqs.q: Who owes the Pennsylvania transfer tax in Easton?
faqs.a: Under state law both the person giving the deed and the person receiving it are liable for the 1% state tax. Your sales agreement decides how the cost is divided, and the Recorder of Deeds collects any local share with it.

faqs.q: Is a tenant a problem when selling in Easton?
faqs.a: No, but paperwork matters. The city expects owners who rent to keep tenant names and addresses on file with the Rental Licensing Officer, so give the buyer the lease and those records.

faqs.q: Where does a deed get recorded for an Easton property?
faqs.a: At the Northampton County Recorder of Deeds, which records deeds and mortgages and collects the fees and taxes due on transfers. The office number is (610) 829-6210.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited Easton house?
faqs.a: Yes. Pennsylvania exempts property passed by will or intestate succession from realty transfer tax, and a fiduciary selling for an estate falls outside the seller disclosure chapter. Settle title questions with the estate's attorney before setting a closing date.
